q: Scientific research and the development of new tools and techniques have undoubtedly improved the ____ of our lives.
e: Scientific research and the development of new tools and techniques have undoubtedly improved the quality of our lives. That missing piece is quality.

q: Biology being the study of living things help us to understand every ____.
e: Biology being the study of living things help us to understand every organism. That missing piece is organism.

q: Fields such as genetics and evolution give insight into the past and can help shape the ____.
e: Fields such as genetics and evolution give insight into the past and can help shape the future. That missing piece is future.

q: Agriculture is defined to produce commodities which maintain life, including foods, fibers, forest products, agricultural crops, horticultural crops, and their related ____.
e: Agriculture is defined to produce commodities which maintain life, including foods, fibers, forest products, agricultural crops, horticultural crops, and their related services. The blank is services.

q: Myanmar's agricultural exports include rice, maize, blackgram, greengram, pigeonpea, chickpea, sesame, onion, tamarind, raw ____, vegetables, and fruits.
e: Myanmar's agricultural exports include rice, maize, blackgram, greengram, pigeonpea, chickpea, sesame, onion, tamarind, raw rubber, vegetables, and fruits. Write rubber in the gap.

q: Commercially cultivating agricultural crops in Myanmar are mainly cereals, pulses and ____ crops.
e: Commercially cultivating agricultural crops in Myanmar are mainly cereals, pulses and oilseed crops. Write oilseed in the gap.

q: Rice (Oryza sativa) production is based on its environment, resulting in rain fed lowland rice, winter rice, deep-water rice, upland rice and ____ rice.
e: Rice (Oryza sativa) production is based on its environment, resulting in rain fed lowland rice, winter rice, deep-water rice, upland rice and irrigated rice. That missing piece is irrigated.

q: There are two dominant rice production systems: rain fed lowland and ____ lowland.
e: There are two dominant rice production systems: rain fed lowland and irrigated lowland. Write irrigated in the gap.

q: The traditional method for cultivating rice is ____ the fields while, or after, setting the young seedlings.
e: The traditional method for cultivating rice is flooding the fields while, or after, setting the young seedlings. Write flooding in the gap.

q: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a grass widely cultivated for its seeds, a cereal grain that is a worldwide ____ food.
e: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a grass widely cultivated for its seeds, a cereal grain that is a worldwide staple food. That missing piece is staple.

q: The zero-tillage technique is a new method of wheat cultivation that is used in the Rice-____ cropping system.
e: The zero-tillage technique is a new method of wheat cultivation that is used in the Rice-wheat cropping system. Write wheat in the gap.

q: Maize (Zea mays) is a tropical plant that prefers warm ____ weather.
e: Maize (Zea mays) is a tropical plant that prefers warm humid weather. The blank is humid.

q: Maize seeds are sown with dibbling or ____ method depending on purposes of sowing, types of maize, varieties and farm conditions.
e: Maize seeds are sown with dibbling or drilling method depending on purposes of sowing, types of maize, varieties and farm conditions. That missing piece is drilling.

q: Among the ASEAN countries, Myanmar is the leading pulse and ____ producer.
e: Among the ASEAN countries, Myanmar is the leading pulse and bean producer. That missing piece is bean.

q: Globally, Myanmar is the third-largest producer of pulses after India and ____.
e: Globally, Myanmar is the third-largest producer of pulses after India and canada. Write canada in the gap.

q: Horticulture is a branch of ____.
e: Horticulture is a branch of agriculture. Write agriculture in the gap.

q: The word "horticulture" is derived from the Latin words 'hortus' and 'cultura', which mean 'garden' and '____'.
e: The word "horticulture" is derived from the Latin words 'hortus' and 'cultura', which mean 'garden' and 'cultivation'. That missing piece is cultivation.

q: Olericulture is the vegetable growing, dealing with the culture of non-woody (____) plants for foods.
e: Olericulture is the vegetable growing, dealing with the culture of non-woody (herbaceous) plants for foods. That missing piece is herbaceous.

q: Pomology or Fruticulture is the production of fruits and ____.
e: Pomology or Fruticulture is the production of fruits and nuts. That missing piece is nuts.

q: Viticulture is the production of ____.
e: Viticulture is the production of grapes. Write grapes in the gap.

q: Floriculture is the growing and marketing of flowers and ornamental plants for ____.
e: Floriculture is the growing and marketing of flowers and ornamental plants for floristry. Write floristry in the gap.

q: Turf Management is the production and upkeep of turf, artificial and live, for use in ____.
e: Turf Management is the production and upkeep of turf, artificial and live, for use in recreation. The blank is recreation.

q: Arboriculture is the cultivation and care of individual trees, shrubs, vines, and other perennial ____ plants.
e: Arboriculture is the cultivation and care of individual trees, shrubs, vines, and other perennial woody plants. That missing piece is woody.

q: Landscape Horticulture is the selection, production and care of plants used in landscape ____.
e: Landscape Horticulture is the selection, production and care of plants used in landscape architecture. The blank is architecture.

q: Postharvest Physiology is the management of harvested horticultural crops to determine the best storage and transportation conditions to optimize ____ life after harvest.
e: Postharvest Physiology is the management of harvested horticultural crops to determine the best storage and transportation conditions to optimize shelf life after harvest. Write shelf in the gap.

q: Hydroponics is a method of growing plants without ____.
e: Hydroponics is a method of growing plants without soil. That missing piece is soil.

q: Hydroponics uses less ____ than traditional soil-based systems.
e: Hydroponics uses less water than traditional soil-based systems. That missing piece is water.

q: Hydroponics is a type of horticulture and a subset of hydroculture which involves growing plants, usually crops, without soil, by using water-based mineral ____ solutions in aqueous solvents.
e: Hydroponics is a type of horticulture and a subset of hydroculture which involves growing plants, usually crops, without soil, by using water-based mineral nutrient solutions in aqueous solvents. That missing piece is nutrient.

q: The nutrients used in hydroponic systems can come from many different sources, including fish excrement, duck manure, purchased chemical fertilizers, or artificial nutrient ____.
e: The nutrients used in hydroponic systems can come from many different sources, including fish excrement, duck manure, purchased chemical fertilizers, or artificial nutrient solutions. That missing piece is solutions.

q: Arabidopsis, which serves as a model organism in plant science and ____, is commonly grown hydroponically.
e: Arabidopsis, which serves as a model organism in plant science and genetics, is commonly grown hydroponically. That missing piece is genetics.

q: Aquaculture, also known as aquafarming, is the farming of aquatic organisms such as fish, crustaceans, molluscs, algae and other aquatic ____.
e: Aquaculture, also known as aquafarming, is the farming of aquatic organisms such as fish, crustaceans, molluscs, algae and other aquatic plants. Write plants in the gap.

q: Farming implies some sort of intervention in the rearing process to enhance production, such as regular stocking, feeding, protection from ____, etc.
e: Farming implies some sort of intervention in the rearing process to enhance production, such as regular stocking, feeding, protection from predators, etc. The blank is predators.

q: Fish farming or pisciculture involves commercial breeding of fish, usually for food, in fish tanks or artificial enclosures such as fish ____.
e: Fish farming or pisciculture involves commercial breeding of fish, usually for food, in fish tanks or artificial enclosures such as fish ponds. The blank is ponds.

q: Worldwide, the most important fish species used in fish farming are, in order, carp, salmon, tilapia and ____.
e: Worldwide, the most important fish species used in fish farming are, in order, carp, salmon, tilapia and catfish. The blank is catfish.

q: Mariculture or marine farming is a specialized branch of aquaculture involving the cultivation of marine organisms for food and other animal products in enclosed sections of the open ____.
e: Mariculture or marine farming is a specialized branch of aquaculture involving the cultivation of marine organisms for food and other animal products in enclosed sections of the open ocean. The blank is ocean.

q: Shrimp farming is an aquaculture business that exists in either a marine or freshwater environment, producing shrimp or prawns for human ____.
e: Shrimp farming is an aquaculture business that exists in either a marine or freshwater environment, producing shrimp or prawns for human consumption. The blank is consumption.

q: Algaculture is the farming of algae species including microalgae and ____.
e: Algaculture is the farming of algae species including microalgae and macroalgae. The blank is macroalgae.

q: Integrated fish farming is a system of producing fish in combination with other agricultural or livestock farming operations centered on the fish ____.
e: Integrated fish farming is a system of producing fish in combination with other agricultural or livestock farming operations centered on the fish pond. That missing piece is pond.

q: The term "Livestock" refers to any domesticated, land-living animal that is raised to provide resources like meat, milk, eggs, and feathers, or to provide services like transportation or cultivation ____.
e: The term "Livestock" refers to any domesticated, land-living animal that is raised to provide resources like meat, milk, eggs, and feathers, or to provide services like transportation or cultivation assistance. Write assistance in the gap.

q: The most common livestock animals are cattle, sheep, goat, pig, horse, chicken, and ____.
e: The most common livestock animals are cattle, sheep, goat, pig, horse, chicken, and duck. Write duck in the gap.

q: Manure can be spread on fields to increase crop ____.
e: Manure can be spread on fields to increase crop yields. Write yields in the gap.

q: Animals such as horses, donkey, and yaks can be used for mechanical ____.
e: Animals such as horses, donkey, and yaks can be used for mechanical energy. That missing piece is energy.

q: The grazing of livestock is sometimes used as a way to control weeds and ____.
e: The grazing of livestock is sometimes used as a way to control weeds and undergrowth. Write undergrowth in the gap.

q: Livestock are key drivers for sustainable development in ____.
e: Livestock are key drivers for sustainable development in agriculture. That missing piece is agriculture.

q: Food is one of the major requirements of ____.
e: Food is one of the major requirements of life. Write life in the gap.

q: Plant only is able to manufacture food through the process of ____.
e: Plant only is able to manufacture food through the process of photosynthesis. Write photosynthesis in the gap.

q: Heat or energy producing food such as carbohydrates and ____.
e: Heat or energy producing food such as carbohydrates and fats. That missing piece is fats.

q: Protective food such as vitamins and some ____.
e: Protective food such as vitamins and some minerals. Write minerals in the gap.

q: The bacterium Lactobacillus helps in the formation of curd from ____.
e: The bacterium Lactobacillus helps in the formation of curd from milk. Write milk in the gap.

q: Yeast, one of the simplest eukaryotes, is used in the process of ____.
e: Yeast, one of the simplest eukaryotes, is used in the process of fermentation. Write fermentation in the gap.

q: Wine is obtained from grapes through a similar ____.
e: Wine is obtained from grapes through a similar process. The blank is process.

q: The microorganisms present in the soil act as a decomposing agent, which assist in the production of the compost from dead and decaying organic ____.
e: The microorganisms present in the soil act as a decomposing agent, which assist in the production of the compost from dead and decaying organic matter. Write matter in the gap.

q: Pharmacognosy is a name derived from Greek words, which mean drug and ____.
e: Pharmacognosy is a name derived from Greek words, which mean drug and knowledge. Write knowledge in the gap.

q: About 80% of world population is still using natural product for their primary healthcare ____.
e: About 80% of world population is still using natural product for their primary healthcare needs. That missing piece is needs.

q: The chief ingredient of aspirin, salicylic acid, was originally obtained from the bark of ____ tree.
e: The chief ingredient of aspirin, salicylic acid, was originally obtained from the bark of willow tree. That missing piece is willow.

q: The bark of cinchona tree, Cinchona sp., contains quinine a drug used to treat ____.
e: The bark of cinchona tree, Cinchona sp., contains quinine a drug used to treat malaria. Write malaria in the gap.

q: Digitalis, which is used in treatment of heart disease, is obtained from the leaves of foxglove plant, Digitalis ____.
e: Digitalis, which is used in treatment of heart disease, is obtained from the leaves of foxglove plant, Digitalis purpurea. The blank is purpurea.

q: Periwinkle, Catharanthus sp. is the source of two drugs that are effective against Hodgkin disease and some ____.
e: Periwinkle, Catharanthus sp. is the source of two drugs that are effective against Hodgkin disease and some leukemia. That missing piece is leukemia.

q: Two powerful pain relieved compounds, morphine and codeine are extracted from opium poppy, Papaver ____.
e: Two powerful pain relieved compounds, morphine and codeine are extracted from opium poppy, Papaver somniferum. The blank is somniferum.

q: Over 50% of commercially available drugs are based on bioactive compounds extracted from non-human ____.
e: Over 50% of commercially available drugs are based on bioactive compounds extracted from non-human species. That missing piece is species.

q: The healing of human minor illness by using therapies based on medicines obtained from animals or ultimately derived from them is known as ____.
e: The healing of human minor illness by using therapies based on medicines obtained from animals or ultimately derived from them is known as zootherapy. The blank is zootherapy.

q: The leech, Hirudo medicinalis, is approved by the Food and Drug Administration for medical ____.
e: The leech, Hirudo medicinalis, is approved by the Food and Drug Administration for medical use. That missing piece is use.

q: While the leech feeding on the surface of the skin, they also secrete anti-coagulants which helps to keep the blood ____.
e: While the leech feeding on the surface of the skin, they also secrete anti-coagulants which helps to keep the blood flowing. The blank is flowing.

q: A molecule called bradykinin from the viper venom is found to be related to a class of molecules that stop Angiotensis-Converting Enzymes (ACE) from blocking ____.
e: A molecule called bradykinin from the viper venom is found to be related to a class of molecules that stop Angiotensis-Converting Enzymes (ACE) from blocking bradykinins. The blank is bradykinins.

q: Bradykinins were eventually developed into the drug captopril, used to treat hypertension, cardiac conditions and to preserve kidney functions in ____.
e: Bradykinins were eventually developed into the drug captopril, used to treat hypertension, cardiac conditions and to preserve kidney functions in diabetics. That missing piece is diabetics.

q: Maggots can turn a chronic wound into an acute wound in a matter of days by eating the chronic tissue and ____.
e: Maggots can turn a chronic wound into an acute wound in a matter of days by eating the chronic tissue and bacteria. Write bacteria in the gap.

q: Spider silk is referred to by many scientists as bio-____.
e: Spider silk is referred to by many scientists as bio-steel. That missing piece is steel.

q: Spider silk can also be used to make artificial ligaments and tendons that support tissue, bone and nerve ____.
e: Spider silk can also be used to make artificial ligaments and tendons that support tissue, bone and nerve cells. The blank is cells.

q: The spider silk gene for the silk protein is connected to DNA in the mammary gland of ____.
e: The spider silk gene for the silk protein is connected to DNA in the mammary gland of goat. That missing piece is goat.

q: Humans make calcitonin, a hormone that inhibits bone loss, in the thyroid ____.
e: Humans make calcitonin, a hormone that inhibits bone loss, in the thyroid gland. That missing piece is gland.

q: The synthetic version of this calcitonin from the coho salmon, the calcitonin-salmon, can be used to treat people with calcium regulation ____.
e: The synthetic version of this calcitonin from the coho salmon, the calcitonin-salmon, can be used to treat people with calcium regulation disorders. Write disorders in the gap.

q: Every person in the world today, who receives vaccines, antibiotics, or implanted medical devices such as pacemakers, has had their safety ensured by the blue blood of the horseshoe ____.
e: Every person in the world today, who receives vaccines, antibiotics, or implanted medical devices such as pacemakers, has had their safety ensured by the blue blood of the horseshoe crab. The blank is crab.

q: A protein in the blood called Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) reacts to all kinds of microorganisms and can easily detect dangerous endotoxins that cause fever and can be ____.
e: A protein in the blood called Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) reacts to all kinds of microorganisms and can easily detect dangerous endotoxins that cause fever and can be fatal. Write fatal in the gap.

q: You wear breathable cotton clothes in summers that are obtained from ____.
e: You wear breathable cotton clothes in summers that are obtained from plants. Write plants in the gap.

q: Structurally, plant fibres are sclerenchymatous cells and are parts of the plant ____.
e: Structurally, plant fibres are sclerenchymatous cells and are parts of the plant skeleton. That missing piece is skeleton.

q: The thickening walls are due to deposition of cellulose and ____.
e: The thickening walls are due to deposition of cellulose and lignin. That missing piece is lignin.

q: Cotton, Gossypium spp., is the world's chief fibre ____.
e: Cotton, Gossypium spp., is the world's chief fibre plant. That missing piece is plant.

q: Jute, Corchorus spp., is a very valuable best ____.
e: Jute, Corchorus spp., is a very valuable best fibre. Write fibre in the gap.

q: Jute fibre is the world's chief material for manufacturing textiles in making roofing materials, curtains and gunny ____.
e: Jute fibre is the world's chief material for manufacturing textiles in making roofing materials, curtains and gunny bags. The blank is bags.

q: Sericulture is an agro-based ____.
e: Sericulture is an agro-based industry. The blank is industry.

q: It involves rearing of silkworm moths, Bombyx mori for the production of raw silk, which is the yarn obtained out of ____.
e: It involves rearing of silkworm moths, Bombyx mori for the production of raw silk, which is the yarn obtained out of cocoons. Write cocoons in the gap.

q: Silkworm has four stages in its life cycle: egg, caterpillar (larva), pupa and adult ____.
e: Silkworm has four stages in its life cycle: egg, caterpillar (larva), pupa and adult moth. Write moth in the gap.

q: When the worms hatched, they are called caterpillars which are food specific and eat voraciously on mulberry ____.
e: When the worms hatched, they are called caterpillars which are food specific and eat voraciously on mulberry leaves. That missing piece is leaves.

q: After reaching the complete stage, caterpillars secrete fluid protein called silk and spin cocoon as a protective shell around the ____.
e: After reaching the complete stage, caterpillars secrete fluid protein called silk and spin cocoon as a protective shell around the pupa. That missing piece is pupa.

q: Changing into the adult form from the pupa inside the cocoon is called ____.
e: Changing into the adult form from the pupa inside the cocoon is called metamorphosis. The blank is metamorphosis.

q: Silk is called the "Queen of Textiles" and is known for its qualities like luxury, elegance, class and ____.
e: Silk is called the "Queen of Textiles" and is known for its qualities like luxury, elegance, class and comfort. The blank is comfort.

q: Today, China and India are the two main producers, together manufacturing more than 90% of the world production each ____.
e: Today, China and India are the two main producers, together manufacturing more than 90% of the world production each year. The blank is year.

q: Wool is one of the most widely used animal fibres and mainly harvested by ____.
e: Wool is one of the most widely used animal fibres and mainly harvested by shearing. The blank is shearing.

q: As an animal fibre, wool consists of protein together with a small percentage of ____.
e: As an animal fibre, wool consists of protein together with a small percentage of lipids. The blank is lipids.

q: The quality of wool is determined by its fibre diameter, crimp, yield, color, and staple ____.
e: The quality of wool is determined by its fibre diameter, crimp, yield, color, and staple strength. Write strength in the gap.

q: Fibre diameter is the most important wool characteristic determining quality and ____.
e: Fibre diameter is the most important wool characteristic determining quality and price. Write price in the gap.

q: Wood is an important plant product, which has been in the service of humankind since the dawn of ____.
e: Wood is an important plant product, which has been in the service of humankind since the dawn of civilization. That missing piece is civilization.

q: The unprocessed wood may be used in the form of lumber i.e. wood intended for heavy ____.
e: The unprocessed wood may be used in the form of lumber that is wood intended for heavy construction. The blank is construction.

q: Teak, Tectona grandis; Pyinkado, Xylia dolabriformis are the most valuable of timber yielding plants of ____.
e: Teak, Tectona grandis; Pyinkado, Xylia dolabriformis are the most valuable of timber yielding plants of myanmar. That missing piece is myanmar.
